items.content_html:
Closes #46493

Summary of changes

  1. Clarify srcData: null allocation:
    • In WebGLRenderingContext.texImage2D() and WebGL2RenderingContext.texImage3D(), explicit mention is added that srcData may be null to allocate texture storage without uploading pixels. WebGL implementations initialize this allocated storage to zeros to prevent information leakage.
  2. Correct uncompressed texture parameter descriptions:
    • In texImage2D, texSubImage2D, texImage3D, and texSubImage3D, srcData was described as "containing the compressed texture data". That wording was a copy-paste remnant from compressedTexImage2D / compressedTexImage3D. These methods handle uncompressed image/pixel data, so the description now accurately specifies "containing the image pixel data".

Verification

  • Ran npx prettier -c on all 4 modified files (Passed).
  • Ran npx markdownlint-cli2 on all 4 modified files (Passed — 0 issues).
  • Ran npx cspell on all 4 modified files (Passed — 0 issues).
  • Ran npm test (node --test) — all 27 tests across 4 suites passed (0 failures).
items.title: docs(webgl): clarify srcData allows null to allocate storage and fix uncompressed texture descriptions

Description

This PR adds the page for emulation.setGeolocationOverride command, with corresponding updates to the module overview page and the sidebar.

Note

The Firefox note in BCD explicitly states that the global configuration is not yet supported.
My testing in Chrome shows the same limitation: omitting both scope selectors returns invalid argument: “Either user contexts or browsing contexts must be provided”. However, there's no such note for Chrome in BCD.

The current version of the page aligns with the spec to say that session-wide overrides are applied when neither contexts nor userContexts is specified. Let me know if this needs to be changed to the implemented behaviour instead.

Spec link

  • https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#command-emulation-setGeolocationOverride

items.content_html:
Description

Corrects the code parameter docs for WebSocket.close(). When close() is called without a code, the close frame is sent with no status code, so the server sees 1005 ("No Status Received"), not 1000. The page now also explains that the code of the browser's close event is taken from the server's reply.

Motivation

The page currently says an omitted code is set to 1000 for a normal closure. No code is sent at all. Readers who rely on the current text (for example, checking for 1000 on the server) get unexpected results. The browser-side code also depends on how the server replies, which the page didn't mention.

I verified this in Chrome and Firefox, and with Node's built-in WebSocket, against a raw server that logs the exact close frame it receives:

  • In all cases, the client's close frame had an empty payload (no status code).
  • The close event code mirrors the server's reply: 1005 when the server echoes the empty frame, 1000 when the server replies with 1000, and 1006 (wasClean: false) when the server drops the connection without replying.

Additional details

  • WHATWG WebSockets spec, close(): if neither code nor reason is present, "the WebSocket Close message must not have a body".
  • RFC 6455 §7.1.5: the connection close code is the status code in the first close frame received. If that frame contains no status code, the close code is considered to be 1005.
  • RFC 6455 §5.5.1: an endpoint replying to a close frame typically echoes the status code it received.

Related issues and pull requests

None.
items.title: Fix default close code for WebSocket.close() with no arguments
